hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Adjacent elements can only be swapped if they have an identical number of set bits.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: This partitions the array into contiguous segments where each element within a segment shares the same set bit count.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Elements within each segment can be sorted in any order. For the entire array to be sortable, the maximum value of each segment must be <= the minimum value of the subsequent segment.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def canSortArray(self, nums: list[int]) -> bool:
        prev_max = -1
        i = 0
        n = len(nums)
        while i < n:
            cnt = nums[i].bit_count()
            cur_min = nums[i]
            cur_max = nums[i]
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and nums[j].bit_count() == cnt:
                cur_min = min(cur_min, nums[j])
                cur_max = max(cur_max, nums[j])
                j += 1
            if prev_max > cur_min:
                return False
            prev_max = cur_max
            i = j
        return True
```

complexity.notes: Single pass grouping consecutive elements by bit count.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Bubble sort simulation is O(n^2) when an O(n) segment boundary check suffices.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) extra memory maintaining segment extrema.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize equivalence relation induced by adjacent swaps on identical set bits.
